title: B2B ABM Go-Live: Relationship-Grain Activation Under a Deadline

steps.prompt: An Account-Based Marketing rollout launches in two weeks, where buyers associate one Contact with multiple Accounts. Mapping a true Account-Contact relationship requires data harmonization effort. The CRM architect asks whether mapping Account Contact directly from Contact is sufficient. What should the architect decide?

options.label: Map Account Contact from the Account–Contact relationship object, related to both Account and Individual.
options.rationale: Harmonizing the relationship entity establishes a distinct row for each account-person pairing. Downstream segmentations can then target contacts within their specific organizational roles without losing multi-account context.

options.label: Map Account Contact one-to-one from Contact so modeling finishes today and activation planning starts tomorrow.
options.rationale: Collapsing multiple account associations into a single contact record discards the many-to-many junction grain, making it impossible for marketing activations to determine which account attributes govern each touchpoint.

options.label: Duplicate each Contact record across each Account directly inside the CRM source before ingestion.
options.rationale: Cloning contact rows in core CRM corrupts data hygiene, inflates platform storage, and complicates identity resolution across duplicate external records.

steps.prompt: A custom Account-Contact junction DMO is assigned to the Other category. Recreating it in the Profile category requires rebuilding relationships and re-testing. The admin asks if the junction can remain categorized as Other while being used for Activation Membership. How should the architect guide them?

options.label: Leave the junction in the Other category and rely on its Account and Contact relationships to make it selectable.
options.rationale: The activation engine ignores relationship links when determining eligible membership objects, preventing any DMO in the Other category from serving as an activation anchor.

options.label: Recreate the junction in the Profile category, re-relate it to Account and Contact, and select it for membership.
options.rationale: The platform segmentation and activation engine strictly requires membership entities to belong to the Profile category. Transitioning the junction allows marketing to select it directly as the target activation grain.

options.label: Change the junction category to Engagement to enable streaming event activations to Marketing Cloud.
options.rationale: Engagement category objects represent time-stamped interaction records rather than persistent entity associations, making them unsuitable for defining membership cohorts.

steps.prompt: In an activation dry run, a Contact associated with two Accounts produced only one Data Extension row, dropping the second Account's attributes. Re-segmenting on the junction takes an additional build day. Leadership proposes keeping Contact membership and resolving context inside Marketing Cloud. How should the architect respond?

options.label: Keep Contact as the membership object and look up each Contact's Accounts inside Marketing Cloud journeys.
options.rationale: Delegating relationship reconstruction to Marketing Cloud journey activities introduces complex script queries, increases journey latency, and fails when contacts have ambiguous active accounts.

options.label: Segment on junction rows, set the junction as Activation Membership, and pull Contact attributes through relationships.
options.rationale: Anchoring membership on the junction outputs an independent row for every Account-Contact pairing, preserving distinct company attributes for each relationship when records land in Marketing Cloud.

options.label: Combine multiple Account names into a delimited text string attribute on the unified Contact profile.
options.rationale: Merging distinct structural values into delimited text fields breaks automated journey personalization and prevents targeted filtering on discrete company parameters.

steps.prompt: Compliance requires every Contact Point Email for an Individual to be present in the Marketing Cloud Data Extension, but Max Attribute Values is capped at 1. Building a fan-out transform requires multiple days. The team asks if raising the attribute limit resolves the requirement. How should the architect advise?

options.label: Build a transform that outputs one row per Individual and email, then segment and activate on it.
options.rationale: Generating an unpivoted dataset with one record per address ensures each email address receives a dedicated Data Extension row that Marketing Cloud can individually target.

options.label: Raise Max # of Attribute Values on a custom activation DMO and keep the current membership object.
options.rationale: Increasing attribute value limits packs additional email values as comma-separated entries into a single row, which journey builder cannot parse as distinct recipient targets.

options.label: Configure a scheduled script in Marketing Cloud to split comma-separated emails after every activation sync.
options.rationale: Relying on external SQL queries or scripts to reshape incoming data introduces operational fragility, scheduling delays, and synchronicity gaps between Data Cloud and journey execution.

steps.prompt: Activation fails because three attributes named Id collide across Individual, Contact Point Email, and a Redshift DMO. The integration lead can assign preferred activation names this afternoon, or spend three days rebuilding the Redshift DMO with unique schema fields past go-live. Which approach should the architect direct?

options.label: Assign preferred activation names to colliding Id attributes and re-run the activation today.
options.rationale: Preferred activation names disambiguate field aliases directly within the destination payload without altering underlying data lake schema definitions or jeopardizing delivery milestones.

options.label: Rebuild the Redshift DMO with non-overlapping field names, then re-run the activation after go-live.
options.rationale: Rebuilding underlying data model objects causes significant schedule slippage and invalidates existing mapping dependencies to fix a naming conflict that target-layer alias configuration easily solves.

options.label: Drop conflicting Id attributes from the activation payload and pass only person names.
options.rationale: Omitting primary and foreign identifiers prevents downstream systems from reliably matching and synchronizing profile records back to source platforms.
